questions.q: What's the difference between a stacked column chart and a 100% stacked column chart?
options: A stacked column shows categories as parts of a total; a 100% stacked column shows each category's percentage share of that total
They are the same visual with different names
100% stacked only works with a single category
Stacked columns can't use a Legend, but 100% stacked can
questions.explain: Stacked columns show absolute values stacked together; 100% stacked normalizes every column to represent percentage share instead.

questions.q: What does the 'Next level' drill icon do, compared to selecting a single column and drilling down?
options: It expands every data point to the next level at once, rather than requiring you to select each column individually
It removes the date hierarchy from the chart
It only works on pie charts
It collapses the chart back to its highest level
questions.explain: Selecting one column and drilling down reveals that column's detail. 'Next level' expands all data points to the next level in one action.

questions.q: What is the difference between cross-filtering and cross-highlighting?
options: Cross-filtering hides unrelated data entirely in other visuals; cross-highlighting emphasizes matching data while dimming the rest, without hiding anything
Cross-filtering only works on pie charts; cross-highlighting only works on column charts
They are functionally identical
Cross-highlighting is permanent; cross-filtering can be undone
questions.explain: Cross-filter narrows what's visible; cross-highlight keeps everything visible but emphasizes what matches the selection — useful for comparing a selection against the whole.

questions.q: How do you enable the Filter/Highlight/None interaction icons on visuals in Power BI Desktop?
options: Select a visual, then go to Format > Enable interactions
Right-click the report canvas and select Interactions
They are always on by default with no way to configure them
Only available in the Power BI service, not Desktop
questions.explain: Enable interactions from the Format ribbon shows Filter, Highlight, and None icons on every other visual, letting you set how the selected visual affects each one.

questions.q: When should you avoid a pie or donut chart?
options: When there are more than five or six categories, since it becomes hard to read at a glance
Whenever the data includes any negative values
Whenever more than one measure exists in the model
Pie charts should never be used in a Power BI report
questions.explain: Pie and donut charts work best with a small number of slices — beyond five or six categories, differences between slice sizes become difficult to distinguish.
